Shammah
SHAM-mah
proper noun
Hebrew Shammah, perhaps “astonishment” or “waste,” one of the three chief mighty men of David.

📖 Biblical Definition

Shammah the son of Agee the Hararite was one of the three mightiest of David’s mighty men, remembered for a single deed of valour at a piece of ground full of lentils. The Philistines gathered into a troop where the ground was, and the people fled before them; but Shammah stood in the midst of the ground, and defended it, and slew the Philistines, and the LORD wrought a great victory (2Sa 23:11; 2Sa 23:12). The dictionary marks Shammah as the man who would not flee. The field was small and the lentils a mean prize, and the rest of the people thought it not worth the risk; but Shammah held his ground, and God gave a great deliverance through one man who would not yield his post. So the Scripture teaches the saint to watch, stand fast in the faith, quit himself like a man, and be strong (1Co 16:13), and having done all, to stand (Eph 6:13). The victory is named the LORD’s, for it was God who wrought it; yet He wrought it through a man who stood when others fled. Shammah is a witness that there is no post so small that God cannot win a great victory there, and that faithfulness in a mean field, held against the foe, may be the occasion of a deliverance for the whole people of God.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

One of David’s three chief mighty men, who alone defended a field of lentils against the Philistines.

expand to see more

SHAMMAH, the son of Agee the Hararite, one of David’s three mighty men.

The Philistines gathered where a piece of ground was full of lentils.

The people fled, but Shammah stood in the midst of the ground.

He defended it and slew the Philistines, and the LORD wrought a great victory.

He is the man who would not flee his post.

📖 Key Scripture

2Sa 23:11 — "And after him was Shammah the son of Agee the Hararite. And the Philistines were gathered together into a troop, where was a piece of ground full of lentiles: and the people fled from the Philistines."

2Sa 23:12 — "But he stood in the midst of the ground, and defended it, and slew the Philistines: and the LORD wrought a great victory."

1Co 16:13 — "Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong."

Eph 6:13 — "Wherefore take unto you the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A figure of Scripture; he shows that God wins great victories through one man who will not flee his post.

expand to see more

Shammah has drawn no redefinition from the present age, surviving as a name in the roll of David’s mighty men. The dictionary records him that the reader may mark the single deed of valour for which the Scripture honours him.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is faithfulness in a small post held against the foe. The field of lentils was a mean prize, and the people fled; but Shammah stood, and the LORD wrought a great victory through him. So the saint is bidden to stand fast in the faith and, having done all, to stand. There is no post so small that God cannot win a great deliverance there; and the man who holds his ground when others flee may be the occasion of salvation for the whole people of God.
